name: today
description: one day's work (946db82..7064c3b, 2026-07-30) read back by a tiered swarm: does the machinery do what its own docstrings claim
_scope: The 30 tracked .py files changed by the four commits 15fbcd2, 536f91e, 967c7c3, 7064c3b -- 10515 insertions. Listed literally rather than globbed, so the spec records exactly what 'today's work' was and a rerun measures the same set.
_why_this_target: Most of this code is a policy mechanism: it claims to enforce a constitution it cannot itself verify. Docstring-versus-code is therefore the highest-value lens available, and it is the one the scan tier already runs. Three defects found by hand in this same code (a test sourcing its baseline from live HEAD, a repair command the guard denies, a directory rule that blocks the narrow command and permits the broad one) are the calibration: a swarm that finds none of them found nothing.

tiers.name: scan
tiers.intro:
FILE: {module}  (chunk {index} of {total}, starting at line {first_line})

This file was written or substantially rewritten in a single day. Much of this codebase is machinery that ENFORCES a policy -- guards, gates, contracts, hooks, inventories. For that kind of code the gap between what a docstring promises and what the code does is not a documentation defect; it is the failure itself, because the docstring is what everyone downstream believes.

tiers.name: research
tiers.intro: You have {inputs} independent scan reports covering one day's work on the Daedalus agent kernel: a canonical contract layer (schemas, artifact store, effect-boundary inventory), a policy guard with its git hooks and its own test suite, a grounding checker for model-authored reports, and a fan-out funnel tool. They were written together and land together.
tiers.task:
Find what spans them. A defect that lives in one file is the scan tier's job; yours is the pattern that only appears once you hold several files at once -- a contract declared in one module and enforced differently in another, a guarantee whose test is in a file that cannot observe it, two modules disagreeing about what a term means, a check whose bypass lives elsewhere.

State each cross-file pattern as a hypothesis with a refutation condition: name the observation that would kill it. Every path and symbol you cite in `evidence` must be one you actually saw in the reports above -- an invented reference cannot be checked and will be discarded.

tiers.name: review
tiers.intro: You have {inputs} hypotheses produced by a research tier over one day's work on the Daedalus kernel. Attack each one. A hypothesis carrying `raised_independently_by: N` was reached by N research groups that could not see each other -- weigh that as weak corroboration of the OBSERVATION, never of the EXPLANATION, since they shared a prior and the same scan reports.
tiers.task:
Each hypothesis carries `cited_source`: the ACTUAL source at the references it cites, read from the repository just now. Judge against that source, not against the hypothesis's description of it -- the description is what you are testing. If `cited_source` says NOT FOUND IN REPOSITORY or NOT PRESENT IN FILE, the hypothesis rests on evidence that does not exist and is refuted on that ground alone; say so and move on.

One failure mode is specific to this target and you should expect it: this code is full of deliberate, documented limitations -- an inventory row marked UNGUARDED, a contract whose docstring says it does not authenticate anyone, a guard that says in its own text that it is not a security boundary. A hypothesis that rediscovers a stated limitation and reports it as a discovery is refuted: the code already says it. What is NOT refuted is a limitation the code does not admit to.

For each: the strongest counterargument first, then whether it survives, then the narrowest surviving form, then the concrete check that would settle it. Default to refuted when uncertain.

tiers.name: plan
tiers.intro: You have {inputs} reviewed findings about one day's work on the Daedalus kernel. The reviewer already discarded what it refuted; these survived.
tiers.task:
Turn the survivors into ordered work. Every step names a file from the repository index and the check that proves it worked.

Paths are not negotiable: copy a path only if it appears in your input or in the repository index above, and answer UNKNOWN otherwise. UNKNOWN is a correct answer; an invented path only looks actionable.

One constraint on your ordering that is real and not stylistic: some of these files are PROTECTED policy artifacts (docs/IKARUS_ARIADNE_MASTER_PLAN.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, daedalus/config.py, daedalus/sensitivity.py, daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py, tools/iron_plan_guard.py, tools/iron_plan_hook_runner.py, tests/test_iron_plan_guard.py, .githooks/*, .github/*). A change to one of those is not an ordinary task -- it requires an owner-approved amendment. Mark every step that touches one, so the plan does not read as if they were all the same kind of work.
